# Discussion

**Main finding.** A sparse intervention produces large article--noun rewrites,
but the six-cell split shows that the generated article carries them. For S1
at \(5\times\), treated-article replay reproduces the new top noun on 20/20
prompts; \(\operatorname{cosine}(E_M,E_T)=0.95\), while matched-prefix
leftover TV is \(0.028\) and comparable to a random control.

Across a gain change below \(0.004\), fixed-article distributions move only
\(0.014\) TV while the free-path noun distribution jumps \(0.938\) TV in
near-perfect token-substitution alignment. Discrete decoding is therefore a
high-gain causal relay; behavioral magnitude need not measure persistent
latent control.

This is a **transmission** result, not evidence that no latent plan exists.
Representation at \(P\) and transmission of its later effect are distinct;
the assay separates generated-token relay from matched-prefix leftover, not
fused packages from modular plans.

**Replay as a falsifier.** If the article carries the later change, replaying
it in an unintervened run should recreate that change [@chan2022scrubbing].
It does; \(E_T=E_M+E_R\) makes this an exact vector split.

**Two causal registers.** A generated position contains both a public token
identity and a private contextual state [@shih2026registers]. Our
target-constructed residual patch shows that lexical influence can survive
from the pre-article position under an identical visible article, while S1
shows that a natural sparse intervention can be overwhelmingly relayed through
the public token. These are a real-model double phenotype, not a double
dissociation between comparable natural sparse mechanisms: the patch is target
constructed and subthreshold. The routes also interact, precluding a general
additive allocation percentage.

**Closed loop.** The generated article is self-generated feedback. We borrow
the intervention logic of opening a biological feedback loop—replay the
consequence, restore its baseline value under perturbation, and cross public
feedback with private state—not an anatomical analogy to nervous systems.

**Methodological standard.** Multi-token causal claims should report the six
cells, exact vector split, both fixed-token leftovers, and intervention-off
token contrast; use full-sequence recomputation and target-free distances; and
validate reachability and sensitivity. Otherwise a later-token change shows
coordinated output, not identified leftover control.
